subject: MSA / Order Form — third-party OSS liability carve-outs and aggregate damages scope
messages:
From: Nora Kim <nora.kim@datavault.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@datavault.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — OSS liability and damage caps

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the call today. Attached are our redlines to the MSA and the Order Form (PDF + comments). Our legal team flagged two items that are blockers for procurement:

1) OSS / third-party software: we need a pass-through indemnity for open-source/model licenses where DataVault is forced to remediate or incur licensing claims because of a third-party model/component you ship (e.g., open-source model weights, tokenizers bundled by Redwood). We requested a limited pass-through obligation limited to direct costs and remediation fees, not unlimited indemnity.

2) Limitation of liability and damages: we proposed a carve-out for damages arising from third-party IP claims and a narrow consequential damages carve-out tied to data exfiltration. We also requested the Order Form aggregate cap be at 2x annual fees for the first year of the agreement given volume.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept a capped OSS pass-through (we proposed $250k per claim / $750k aggregate) and to what extent you can narrow consequential damages exceptions. Our team is flexible on language if Redwood provides a reasonable set of guardrails.

Attachments: DataVault_MSA_redlines.pdf, OrderForm_DL_redlines.docx

Can you loop your contracts/ops folks in? I copied legal@datavault.com.

Best,
Nora
Nora Kim
Senior Counsel, DataVault Analytics
N: 415-555-0192

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nora Kim <nora.kim@datavault.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — OSS liability and damage caps

Nora — thanks for the detailed redlines and for surfacing the specific numbers. Looping in Laura (Head of Contracts) and Rishi (Legal Ops) to weigh in on the passthrough request.

High-level from Sales: we understand procurement needs protection for third-party OSS model claims. We have two preferred approaches we can discuss:

- Option A (preferred for speed): Redwood accepts a limited OSS pass-through indemnity, but with a conditional cap tied to fees paid under the Order Form (e.g., min($250k, 2x fees paid in prior 12 months)) and with an explicit process for remediation and vendor acceptance before costs are reimbursable.

- Option B (if indemnity not acceptable): Redwood offers an extended warranty + expedited remediation SLA for OSS components and a contribution to remediation costs up to a defined cap, but no traditional indemnity.

On consequential damages carve-outs: we can accept a narrow carve-out for data exfiltration and IP claims, but need to exclude speculative downstream business interruption claims.

Laura / Rishi — any initial redline language you want me to propose back to DataVault?

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive — Strategic Deals, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nora Kim <nora.kim@datavault.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 14:26:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — OSS liability and damage caps

Ben / Nora — thanks for flagging. I reviewed DataVault's redlines. Key points from our contracts/legal side: 

- We cannot accept unlimited pass-through indemnity for third-party OSS claims. However, we are open to a narrowly scoped pass-through where Redwood agrees to (i) use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate or replace the infringing OSS component and (ii) reimburse documented, reasonable remediation costs up to a defined monetary cap.

- Proposed redline language (summary): "For third-party open-source software or model licenses where a claim arises directly from software shipped by Redwood as part of the Service, Redwood will (a) use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate or replace the component, and (b) reimburse Customer for documented, reasonable remediation costs incurred by Customer up to $250,000 per claim and $750,000 aggregate during any 12-month period, provided Customer first allows Redwood to attempt remediation and the costs are pre-approved in writing."

- Limitation of Liability: we propose the Order Form cap be 3x annual fees (or $1M, whichever is greater) for the first 12 months for commercial customers. We can be flexible on the multiplier based on term and deployment model.

- Consequential damages: we will accept carve-outs for third-party IP claims and confirmed data breaches caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. We will push back on broad consequential damage exceptions that include lost profits from indirect causes.

Please confirm if DataVault can accept the remediation-first requirement and the $250k / $750k caps. If they can, we will prepare tracked redlines back to the MSA and Order Form.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: Nora Kim <nora.kim@datavault.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@datavault.com
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — OSS liability and damage caps

Laura — thanks, that language is helpful and gets us much closer. A couple follow-ups from our counsel: 

- The remediation-first requirement is acceptable, but DataVault needs some standby remediation rights: if Redwood does not commence remediation within 30 days or fails to make demonstrable progress, DataVault may pursue remediation and submit documented costs for reimbursement up to the cap.

- Dollar caps: we were asking for $250k per claim / $750k aggregate as a baseline; your 3x annual fees option could be OK but we prefer a fixed-dollar safety net for OSS claims given potential outsized IP litigation costs. Can you confirm Redwood will accept $250k / $750k as a mutual agreement fallback if 3x fees is materially lower?

- Consequential damages carve-out: we still need to preserve a narrowly tailored consequential damages carve-out to cover third-party IP indemnities (i.e., if DataVault is held liable to its customers because of an IP claim related to Redwood-delivered materials). We can limit recovery to direct monetary obligations DataVault pays to third parties (no speculative loss).

If you can accept the remediation timeline and the fixed-dollar fallback, we can instruct our procurement team to move to track-changes with your redlines.

Best,
Nora

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nora Kim <nora.kim@datavault.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — third-party OSS liability carve-outs and aggregate damages scope (next steps)

Nora / Laura / Rishi — quick internal summary and proposed next steps so we're aligned before we exchange tracked changes: 

1) Redwood will prepare tracked redlines to the MSA and Order Form adopting Laura's remediation-first clause, with explicit pre-approval and documentation requirements for remediation costs.

2) Redwood will include standby rights for the Customer to remediate after a 30-day remediation window if Redwood does not materially progress (per DataVault request).

3) Monetary caps: Redwood proposes: default Order Form cap = greater of (3x annual fees, $1,000,000). For OSS pass-through specifically, Redwood will accept a fixed-dollar fallback of $250,000 per claim / $750,000 aggregate during any 12-month period, provided the remediation-first and pre-approval conditions are satisfied.

4) Consequential damages carve-outs: Redwood will accept carve-outs narrowly limited to (a) third-party IP claims that result in direct monetary obligations, and (b) confirmed data breaches resulting from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. No carve-outs for speculative downstream business losses.

Action items: Laura & Rishi to produce tracked redlines to the MSA + Order Form reflecting the bullets above. Ben will share the resulting documents with DataVault procurement and legal once ready.

Ben
Account Executive — Strategic Deals, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: DataVault_MSA_redlines.pdf, OrderForm_DL_redlines.docx
